newsitem.title: UK: UK Major says EU on shaky ground over beef.
newsitem.headline: UK Major says EU on shaky ground over beef.

text.p: British Prime Minister John Major said on Wednesday the European Union (EU) was on shaky scientific ground over its banning British beef imports.
"I think the Commission and the European Union are on very shaky scientific ground," Major told BBC radio.
He said there was now more information on transmission of BSE and the Anderson report which suggested action taken in the late 1980s was more comprehensive in eradicating BSE than had been imagined.
"They are fresh issues that need proper discussion with the European Union," he said.

"I can tell you that we will not delay decisions and when we take the decision, we will take it on the basis of public health, on the basis of common sense and in the interests of the beef farmer," he added.
"But there are still discussions to be had before that decision can be finally taken."
Asked if he was still pressing for a timetable for lifting the ban, Major said a timetable had always depended on events.
"What we need to be certain (about), is that if the events that were agreed are carried out, that the ban will be lifted. That does need to be certain."
